what: Proof of function: the tokens an agent reads with the open sea and without it (https://mareliberum.dev/proof)

bench.ua: MareLiberum-ProofBench/1.0 (+https://mareliberum.dev/proof; reads each page of a published task set once to count its tokens; follows robots.txt)
bench.ranFrom: a Claude Code session machine (cloud sandbox, through its egress proxy); the brain from a local node of fix-lean/1 on 127.0.0.1:8121

tokenizers.models: OpenAI GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, o-series and GPT-5 models
Anthropic Claude 1 and 2; for Claude 3 and later only "a very rough approximation" (Anthropic)

taskSet.rule: shopping: the pathways GET /brain lists as the strongest (field top, 24 at pick time), kept when confirmed (more worked than failed reports), at most one per site, at most 24; everyday: questions asked at the brain (the record of the doors, 23 and 24 November 2026) and common reads of coding agents, with the page a person would expect an agent to open (chosen by hand; pages whose robots.txt forbids reading, or that a bot wall closes, were not chosen)

method.run: local run of fix-lean/1 before deploy: the lean reader with the fixes for the verifier of 3.33.0
method.robots: robots.txt is read once per host and obeyed for the token MareLiberum-ProofBench (RFC 9309: a 4xx answer allows everything, a 5xx answer or no answer forbids everything); a page the sea's reader is asked not to read (token MareLiberum-Reader) is left out too
method.html: the page as the server sent it, decoded as UTF-8, at most 2.5 MB
method.walls: a page that answers with a bot wall instead of itself (a challenge, a captcha, a request to enable JavaScript) is not counted; the run says so in its row
method.text: readability-style extraction (tools/proof-bench.mjs, extractText): scripts, styles, form controls, hidden elements, nav, aside and footer elements and boxes whose class or id names navigation, menus, headers, footers, sidebars, comments, cookies, sharing or ads are dropped; every paragraph-like block of 25 characters or more scores its parent (1 + commas + one point per 100 characters, at most 3) and, at half and a sixth, the elements above; a box scores more for words like article, content, main, product, post or text in its class or id and less for the words above; the score is reduced by the share of text in links; the best box and its siblings that score at least a fifth of it are the article; like Readability it tries again with fewer rules when an attempt finds less than 500 characters (without dropping unlikely boxes, then without weighing class names) and keeps the longest attempt; a box that holds the page's main or article element is never dropped; the text is written out one block per line, without link targets, markup or images
method.readability: Mozilla Readability 0.6.0 (the library behind Firefox Reader View) on a linkedom document: the text of the article it finds, whitespace collapsed the same way; a cross-check of the extraction above, where it is installed
method.markdown: the Markdown of the sea's reader, digest in node/reader.mjs (the code that answers /r/ and read_page; since 3.33.0 the lean reader of node/lean.mjs: the main part only, a product's essentials first, links once and short), on the same copy of the page; not cut (the reader itself cuts at 60,000 characters, see served)
method.prior: the Markdown of the reader of an earlier release (toMarkdown in node/reader.mjs of the commit named in bench.prior), on the same copy of the page: the reader before and after, page by page, without the page changing in between
method.served: the answer of the sea's /r/ door for the page (a few lines about the page and the sea around the Markdown), rendered by the node's own route on the same copy of the page on the bench machine; on mareliberum.dev it can also list up to three pathways other agents walked to the site
method.servedFull: the /r/ answer with format=full: the long lines around the Markdown as the reader wrote them before 3.33.0 (pathways, the site check, Angel, the brief), rendered the same way
method.brainCompact: the brain's short answer, GET /brain?q=<task>&fmt=compact (since 3.33.0): the confirmed pathways with one line of reason each and the one next step; counted only where the sea answered in that shape
method.mcp: the text block of the answer of the MCP tool read_page (open door /mcp), rendered the same way; it carries the Markdown and a list of the page's links
method.keeps: at least two thirds of the words of its heading (the first h1 inside its main or article element, else the first h1 a person sees, else og:title, else the longest part of its title; words of three letters or more) and, on a shop page, a price
method.result: one search result as a search tool hands it to a model: the page's title, its address and a snippet (its meta description, else the start of its text) of at most 160 characters
method.brain: the answer of GET /brain?q=<task> (and with &fmt=compact) as a local node of the branch fix-lean/1 serves it (127.0.0.1:8121, long memory off, its public address set to https://mareliberum.dev so its links are as long as the live ones), read with the User-Agent MareLiberum-session/1.0; that node's brain holds the 64 pathways the live brain's public answers GET /brain/<task> listed for these 33 tasks on 2026-11-24 (copied with the session's User-Agent, counted nowhere), but not the live node's open index, its current or its other kept state, so its full answers are smaller than the live ones; the short answer carries only pathways and doors, which it has

loop.rule: Anthropic puts simple fact-finding at 3 to 10 tool calls. One of them reads the destination page, which is counted under reading; the others alternate between a search and a page read to judge a result, starting with a search: 3 calls are 1 search and 1 page, 10 calls are 5 searches and 4 pages. A search hands the model 10 results (the page size of the Google Programmable Search API, the default of Exa); one result and one page are as large as the median of this run. Output tokens, reasoning and the re-reading of earlier context in later turns are left out on both sides.

sources.what: Simple fact-finding requires just 1 agent with 3-10 tool calls
sources.by: Anthropic engineering, How we built our multi-agent research system (13 June 2025)

sources.what: The Programmable Search JSON API returns at most 10 results per request (num 1 to 10)
count: 20 by default and at most (a loop on this API reads twice as many results per search)
sources.by: Brave Search API, web search parameters
